views.markdown: Shows the state of the VPN Kill Switch in the status bar. The daemon reports every change, so the symbol follows within a moment.

views.title: Faint question mark
views.text: no state - the daemon is not reporting

views.markdown: The tweak draws its own window above the status bar rather than hooking a private status bar class. That keeps it independent of how Apple rearranges the status bar internally, and it never intercepts touches — the control centre still pulls down over it.

The tweak writes what it does to `/var/mobile/Library/Logs/ggstatus.log`. It records whether it was loaded into SpringBoard, whether it found a window scene, and which state it read.

A faint question mark means the window works and the daemon is silent. Nothing at all means the tweak never got that far — the log says where it stopped.

The symbol sits to the left of the clock. If it collides with something on your device, move it without rebuilding — create `/var/jb/etc/ggstatus.conf` with lines like `X=120`, `Y=14`, `SIZE=20` and respring.

- Moved out from under the battery icon: 0.3.0 sat 6 pt from the right edge, which is exactly where the battery indicator is — the window was there, nothing was visible
- Position and size adjustable via `/var/jb/etc/ggstatus.conf` (`X=`, `Y=`, `SIZE=`) without rebuilding

- The window now has a root view controller. Without one UIKit does not reliably draw a window on recent systems
- The unknown state shows a faint symbol instead of hiding, so a missing state can be told apart from a missing window
- Writes a log to `/var/mobile/Library/Logs/ggstatus.log`
- Falls back to any window scene when none is foreground-active
- Own window above the status bar instead of hooking `_UIStatusBar`, which showed nothing on iOS 18
Without the VPN Kill Switch installed there is no state to show. A respring is needed after installing.
